# How do we measure an autonomous company? A seven-day Anicca log audit

An organization can run hundreds of agents without knowing whether it operates autonomously. A task may require human account setup, recovery, review or delivery. An agent may report a successful run without having produced an outcome that a customer can use. Measuring operational autonomy requires evidence of completed work, not just activity.

**Finding.** We examined one fixed version of Anicca's GitHub activity ledger for November 21–27, 2026 (Japan time). A strict date-prefix parser found 373 lines. Of these, 126 had an explicit DONE status and 116 were unclassified under the chosen status parser. Three of the seven dates had matching lines. These counts describe a log, not unique business tasks, independent successes or an autonomy rate. The gaps are themselves an important baseline.

![Cover: 373 dated log lines, three observed dates, autonomy rate unknown](/assets/research/autonomy-ac01-cover.svg)

## The problem with counting agents

Consider a client project. One agent discovers a job, another prepares a proposal and a third delivers the agreed work. Counting three entries as three completed business outcomes would exaggerate the value delivered. Counting only successful reports would hide failed attempts. And none of those reports proves that a human did not supply credentials or recover a failed step.

Anthropic's [R&D Automation Index](https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development) defines a fixed basket of work and rates degrees of automation. METR's [Time Horizons](https://metr.org/time-horizons/) connects task success probabilities to the duration of tasks for human experts. Both illustrate why an evaluation needs an explicit denominator and evidence of success. Our audit is not a reproduction of either organization's benchmark; it is a first measurement of the observability of our own operations.

## What we actually ran

We pinned the company ACTIVITY.md ledger to Git commit 0bc7ffd051f9f0534b09ccf9382716c7c58c2304. We selected lines beginning with a date from November 21 through November 27, inclusive, optionally preceded by a Markdown list marker. For pipe-delimited records with at least four fields, we classified the third field only when it matched one of our explicit status strings. Unstructured or unfamiliar formats remain unclassified. We calculated exact-text duplicates separately. Normal and optimized Python produced identical JSON receipts.

This method is deliberately conservative. It can miss records in a different format; it cannot determine whether two differently worded reports concern the same task. The input ledger may contain operationally sensitive information, so we publish only aggregate counts, not raw reports, credentials, customer information or personal records. The pinned input, hash, code and receipt are retained in the internal research record.

![Figure 1. Strict date-prefix matches across the seven-day window](/assets/research/autonomy-ac01-days.svg)

Figure 1. 373 lines in a single pinned ledger. Zero on November 21–24 means no matching rows under this parser, not no work. Separate daily documents exist and still need to be reconciled against the ledger without double counting.

| Explicit status classification | Lines |
|---|---:|
| Reported DONE | 126 |
| Reported blocked or failed | 2 |
| Mixed or partial | 2 |
| Other recognized status | 127 |
| Unclassified | 116 |
| Total | 373 |

There was one exact-text duplicate. That does not establish the number of duplicate business tasks. The two explicitly blocked or failed records are not a count of all company failures. Nor does an entry marked DONE establish that an independent verifier accepted the result.

## Designing an operational autonomy metric

The proposed process census separates research, model and evaluation engineering, product development, distribution and sales, client delivery, finance and tax, compute and identity, and governance and recovery. Every process needs a defined frequency, dependency, authorized principal, credential class, required exceptions, task identity and acceptance condition.

Define eligible tasks before observing their outcomes. A verified autonomous completion requires a successful independent receipt and evidence of no routine human intervention. Divide such completions by all eligible tasks due in the window, including failures and unfinished tasks. Missing observations must not be silently promoted to successful outcomes. Report human minutes separately, including setup, account recovery and exception handling. Necessary legal, contractual and safety oversight should be recorded rather than removed to improve an apparent automation score.

![Figure 2. From task identity to independently verified outcome](/assets/research/autonomy-ac01-evidence.svg)

Figure 2. Proposed measurement architecture, not a claim that it is fully deployed. A stable task identifier links attempts, evidence, human involvement and an independently accepted result.

Financial sustainability also needs a different denominator: independently reconciled external receipts against all relevant costs, tax obligations and reserves. Monthly recurring revenue, cash receipts and gross profit measure different things. A directory listing, internal transfer or test payment does not constitute external revenue.

## Applying the measurement to Anicca

The flagship is the Anicca mobile app. Other products and businesses can reuse the same Manager model, ManagerBench and data infrastructure wherever appropriate. But their success conditions differ. Research needs reproducible results; client work needs accepted delivery; a mobile intervention needs measurable benefit and safety; financial operations need settled transactions. An aggregate activity count cannot substitute for any of them.

In this audit we did not establish unique task identities, independent acceptance of every record, human involvement minutes, or current reconciled financial results. Consequently the verified autonomy rate and financial coverage ratio remain unknown. No new model weights, product releases, spending or changes to production permissions occurred. The evidence supports a measurement gap, not a claim of full autonomy.

## What comes next

Recover and reconcile the missing daily records, freeze a complete process inventory, instrument unique task identifiers and link each attempt to verifiable outcomes. Then independently review a defined sample and track both successful and failed work. Once the same measurement can be repeated over a stable task basket, changes in autonomy and economic sustainability can be assessed rather than asserted.

Sources: [Anthropic R&D Automation Index](https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development); [METR Time Horizons](https://metr.org/time-horizons/). All Anicca log counts are from the fixed internal ledger and the audit described above. Outstanding work is tracked in issue #784.
